: 
(per Hon'ble Sri Justice N. Tukaramji) As these appeals are arising out of the selfsame award and the similitude of the facts and law to be considered, we have heard the appeals together and are being decided in this common judgment.
2.

The above appeals are directed against the decree and order dated 22.11.2014 in M.V.O.P.No.470 of 2011 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-XIII Additional Chief Judge (FTC)
City Civil Court, Hyderabad.
3(i) The M.A.C.M.A.No.873 of 2015 has been filed by the claim petitioner seeking enhancement of compensation amount.

Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-XIII Additional Chief Judge (FTC)
City Civil Court, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3(ii) The M.A.C.M.A.No.77 of 2022 has been filed by the owner and driver/respondents 1 and 3 disputing the liability and the quantum awarded.
2 PSKJ&NTRJ Macmas_77_2022,572_2015&873_2015 3(iii) The M.A.C.M.A.No.572 of 2015 has been filed by the insurance company/respondent No.2 disputing the liability and the quantum of compensation.
4. For the facility the appellants are hereinafter referred to with their array in the claim petition.

5. We have heard Mr. K. Hari Mohan Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner, Mr. Srikanth Hariharan, learned counsel for the respondent Nos.1 and 3/owner and driver and Mr. V. Sambasiva Rao, learned counsel for the respondent No.2/insurer.

6. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 09.03.2010 while she was proceeding as pillion rider on motorcycle bearing registration No. AP-09-BE-6239 (for short, 'the motorcycle') with her husband near Rampally village, one Maruthi Car bearing No.AP-29- AJ-4798 (for short, 'the car')
came in rash and negligent manner on wrong side and dashed the motorcycle.
The accident resulted in grievous injuries to herself and her husband/rider of the motorcycle.

The Police, Keesara The National Insurance Co Ltd., vs T Sabitha And 2 Others on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146539228/
1 registered crime and charge sheeted the driver of the car.

sentences.text: Thereupon, the petitioner pleading huge medical expenditure, loss of earnings and complete physical disability, filed petition seeking compensation of Rs.50 lakhs.

The tribunal after due enquiry partly allowed the petition by awarding Rs.38 lakhs with 3 PSKJ&NTRJ Macmas_77_2022,572_2015&873_2015 interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of the petition till realization against the owner, insurer and driver/respondents 1 to 3.

However, directed the insurer/respondent No.2 to pay the awarded amount at the first instance and to recover the same from the owner/respondent No.1.
7.

In appeal, learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that, the tribunal ought to have considered the income claimed by the petitioner through her employment as Tele Caller and also by tailoring but without any reason, notionally fixed annual income at Rs.80,000/-.
Further pleaded that the petitioner had suffered paraplegia due to the injuries suffered in the accident and completely confined to bed.

Having regard to this aspect though the tribunal had considered 100%
disability, in assessment of compensation, failed to include the future prospects.
Additionally, the amounts awarded by the tribunal under conventional heads are on lower side.
Therefore, prayed for reassessment and to award just compensation.

8. Learned counsel for the respondent No.1 and 3/owner and driver would submit that, the tribunal had erred in properly appreciating the materials placed on record especially oral testimony of owner a n d t h e a n o t h e r i n m a t e o f t h e c a r R W - 2 t h a t t h e 4 P S K J & N T R J Macmas_77_2022,572_2015&873_2015 respondent No.3 was the driver of the car at the time of accident and he was holding valid and effective driving licence/Ex.B-2.
In absence of contra evidence, exoneration of the insurer from the liability is unacceptable.

Further, criminal case against the driver in C.C.No.116 of 2011 on the file of the Special Magistrate-II, Cyberabad was ended in acquittal and this fact itself is establishing that there was no rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car in the accident.
That apart, though there was no proof of employment and income, the tribunal erred in fixing the notional income of the petitioner on higher side, in assessment of compensation.
Moreover the amounts awarded for future loss of earnings, future medical expenditure, pain and sufferings, attendant charges and other heads are on higher side without valid basis.
Thus prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.

9. Learned counsel for the respondent No.2/insurer would contend that the tribunal had rightly concluded that there was violation of policy condition and the insurer is not liable to pay compensation.
Having determined the liability, the insurer ought not have been directed to pay the compensation first and recover the same from the owner.
Further contended that the tribunal erred in awarding compensation without considering the contributory 5 PSKJ&NTRJ Macmas_77_2022,572_2015&873_2015 negligence of the motorcycle in the accident.

Furthermore the tribunal should have observed that the rider of the motorcycle is none other than the husband of the insured who did not file driving licence or registration certificate of the motorcycle.
This fact is probabalising the negligent driving of the motorcycle.
The tribunal should have considered the financial position of the owner in restricting the liability to the extent owner only.
Thus prayed for setting aside the direction of pay and recovery in the impugned order.
10. These rival pleas fell for our consideration and we have perused the materials on record.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The accident, involvement of the vehicles, injuries and treatment claimed by the petitioner are not in dispute.

The owner/respondent No.1 raised two fold contentions, firstly, there was no negligent driving of the car in the accident, as such no liability should have been fastened against the car, secondly, the police record erroneously shown the name of Mr. Avunuri Akarsh as driver,
indeed it was the driver/respondent No.3 who was driving the car and he had valid and effective driving licence/Ex.B-2, as such even if any liability is determined, the insurer shall be directed to indemnify.
The petitioner as PW-1 asserted that the car in rash and negligent manner came on wrong side and dashed the motorcycle from rear side.
In cross examination except suggestion, no favourable fact has been elicited.
The police registered crime and charge sheeted the driver of the car.
Howsoever, the owner of the car/respondent No.1 as RW-1 asserted that the acquittal in criminal case is establishing the fact that there was no negligent driving of the car.
Pertinently, in criminal trial, the prosecution has to prove the charge beyond reasonable doubt.
Thus the acquittal may be on the failure of the prosecution to prove any one of the essential factors of the charge.
Further the criminal trial would be against the driver for causing injuries/death by rash or negligent act.
Whereas in the claim petition the rash and negligent driving of the crime vehicle would be considered.
Therefore, mere acquittal of the driver in criminal case cannot be read as conclusive proof that there was no negligent driving of the car in the accident.
In the given factual position and the undisturbed evidence of the injured witness/PW-1, the negligent driving of the car in the accident, as concluded by the tribunal, stands sustained.

13. It has been strenuously contested by the owner/driver/respondent Nos.1 and 3 that the respondent No.3 was 7 PSKJ&NTRJ Macmas_77_2022,572_2015&873_2015 the driver of the car at relevant time and he is holding valid and effective driving licence/Ex.B-2.

Pertinently, the petitioner showing the respondent No.3 as driver of the car filed the claim petition, though the police registered crime and concluded investigation against one Mr.Avunuri Akarsh as the driver of the car.

The petitioner/PW-1 or the respondent No.1 and 3 or the occupant of the car/RW-2 nowhere indicated that, the fact of the respondent No.3 being the driver at relevant time has been brought to the notice of the police or the court concerned at any point of time.
In such factual position, how the petitioner got the details of respondent No.3 as driver is left unexplained.
That apart, the petitioner in her evidence identified the respondent No.3 as the driver of the car who caused the accident.

Interestingly, in the claim petition the owner and the claimed passenger of the car at the time of accident, volunteered and got examined themselves as RWs. 1 and 2 to assert that the respondent No.3 was the driver and that he was holding valid driving licence.

Nonetheless, in absence of any pleading much less any material to show that the respondent Nos.1 and 3had displayed the same bona fide before the police or the criminal court proceedings to place true facts of the accident or to save an innocent person from the rigmarole of criminal trial

, their effort is d e m o n s t r a t i n g t h a t t h e r e s p o n d e n t s h a v e c o n v e n i e n t l y 8 P S K J & N T R J Macmas_77_2022,572_2015&873_2015 pitched tooled statements of the witnesses to meet the adverse material and acceptance of such attempt would amount to paying premium to the doctored moves of the respondents, to set the course for favourable decision in the legal process.

sentences.text: In the aforesaid peculiar circumstances we are convinced that the tribunal had rightly considered the facts in concluding that the plea of respondent No.1 and 3 are far from truth.
Thus the finding of the tribunal on this aspect deserves to be and is accordingly affirmed.

15. In regard to liability, to satisfy the awarded compensation, the record is making out that Mr.
Avunuri Akarsh who had no driving licence was at steering wheel and caused the accident. Further it is not in dispute that the insurance policy covers the liability of the third party.
The violation of policy condition in regard to driving licence is between the insurer/respondent No.2 and the insured/respondent No.1.

In regard to the claim of third party in the back drop of contention of driving licnece of the driver has been set to rest by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Swaran Singh (2004) 3 SCC 297.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Swaran Singh (2004) 3 SCC 297
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus as the evidence is establishing that the driver was not holding valid and effective driving licence and the claimant is third party, directing the insurer to satisfy the award in the 9 PSKJ&NTRJ Macmas_77_2022,572_2015&873_2015 first instance and to recover the same from the insured/respondent No.1 by executing the award is legal and perfectly justified.
Thus this direction of the tribunal in the impugned order is also affirmed.

16. In regard to awarding compensation, in injury cases the Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar v.
Ajay Kumar and another - (2011) 1 SCC 343 has held as follows:
"5.

entities.text:
Raj Kumar v.
Ajay Kumar and another - (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following :

Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage).
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

The National Insurance Co Ltd., vs T Sabitha And 2 Others on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146539228/
4 xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx 13.

sentences.text:
We may now summarise the principles discussed above:
(i) All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity.
(ii) The percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity.

To put it differently, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability (except in a few cases,
where the Tribunal on the basis of evidence, concludes that percentage of loss of earning capacity is the same as percentage of permanent disability).
(iii) The doctor who treated an injured-claimant or who examined him subsequently to assess the extent of his permanent disability can give evidence only in regard the extent of permanent disability.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.

(iv) The same permanent disability may result in different percentages of loss of earning capacity in different persons, depending upon the nature of profession, occupation or job, age, education and other factors."
17.
In the light of the above dictum, the compensation awarded in the present petition needs examination.

18. The treating doctor i.e. Consultant Neuro Surgeon/PW-2 stated that the petitioner/PW-1 suffered multiple injuries and investigation revealed (1) fracture of T-10 vertebra and (2) fracture of right femur and right tibia.

Further stated that PW-1 underwent surgeries of fusion of spine and reduction of right femoral shaft fracture and total traction of spinal cord but it has resulted in complete paralysis of both lower limbs and loss of control on urination and disfunction of the nerves system below D-10 segment of the spinal cord.

Thus the petitioner would be permanently confined t o c h a i r a n d b e d a n d l o s s o f s e n s i b i l i t y a n d c o n t r o l o f 1 1 P S K J & N T R J Macmas_77_2022,572_2015&873_2015 urination.

The doctor estimated complete physical disability and validated the disability certificate/Ex.A-6 and that she may require physiotherapy to the lower limbs, treatment for bed sore and urinary infection as and when arise.
19. This evidence is establishing the physical condition after the treatment and her complete avocational disability.
The petitioner has filed medical bills/Ex.A-14 and physiotherapy receipts/Ex.A-13 for Rs.2,97,096/- and Rs.90,000/- respectively.

Having regard to the injuries and the treatment undergone as per the doctors/PWs.2 and 7, the discharge summaries/Exs.A-3 and A-4, physiotherapist/PW-7, reimbursement of the medical expenses reflected in the bill is found proper.
Accordingly, by rounding of, Rs.3,90,000/- is granted under this head.

5 20.

sentences.text: The doctor/PW-2 deposed about the future possible medical expenses for physiotherapy and treatment for bed sore and urinary infection.
The tribunal, though separately, awarded Rs.10 lakhs under this head.
Having regard to the age of the petitioner and the probable medical necessities including the physiotherapy we enhance the awarded amount to Rs.15,00,000/-.

In regard to loss of earnings during treatment and future earnings, the statements of the doctors are conclusively establishing that the petitioner would be confined to bed with paralysis of both lower limbs.
This physical condition is proving beyond doubt that the earning capacity of the petitioner has been completely shattered.
For this reason 100% disablement in earning capacity shall be taken into account in assessment of compensation.
22. The petitioner has pleaded that she used to earn Rs.8,000/- as Tele Caller in R.K. Solutions and Rs.7,000/- per month through tailoring.
In support the petitioner has placed appointment letter/Ex.A-7, salary certificate/Ex.A-8 and certificate of fashion designing/Ex.A-12.
The employer/PW-6 has validated the documents/Exs:A-7 and A-8 and presented salary receipt/Ex.X-5 for consolidated pay of Rs.8,000/- per month.
However, no document or material has been placed to prove the earnings from tailoring/fashion designing except for the oral claim.

Hence, as the claim and evidence of PW-6, Exs:A-7 and A-8 remained unrebutted, accepting the salary therein i.e.
Rs.8,000/- per month would be proper in assessment of compensation.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pappu Deo Yadav v. V. Naresh Kumar and others 1 has held that the future prospects as enunciated in National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi and others 2 shall be taken into account in assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earnings due to permanent disability.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, considering the age and the nature of employment 40% of the income has to be added towards future prospects.
Thus the annual income of the petitioner would be of Rs.1,34,400/-.

This multiplicand if multiplied with relevant multiplier to the age of petitioner as prescribed in Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another 3 i.e.18, the total comes to Rs.24,19,200/-.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This amount shall be the compensation for complete loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
24. The petitioner also claimed that she had engaged an attendant with salary of Rs.3,500/- to assist her.
Having regard to the fact that the petitioner has to confine to the bed althrough, awarding considerable amount to meet this requirement is found proper.
Accordingly, Rs.10,00,000/- is granted towards attendant charges.
Considering the injuries, medical treatment and the resulted permanent disability, we grant Rs.5,00,000/- towards pain and suffering and Rs.5,00,000/- for the loss of enjoyment of facets of life.

Thus, in all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as under:
 Description

Amount awarded  (In Rupees)
Loss of income due to disability 24,19,200.00
Attendant charges 10,00,000.00
Loss of amenities and enjoyment of life 5,00,000.00
Medical expenses 3,90,000.00
Future medical expenditure 15,00,000.00
Pain and suffering 5,00,000.00

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.63,09,200/- (Rupees sixty three lakhs nine thousand and two hundred only) with interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of the petition till date of realization.
Accordingly the impugned order stands revised.

The respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the differential amount of compensation to the petitioner within four 15 PSKJ&NTRJ Macmas_77_2022,572_2015&873_2015 weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and thereafter may realize the amount from owner/respondent No.1 by executing the award.
On such deposit, the petitioner is permitted to withdraw the entire amount of compensation.

28. In the result, (a) the M.A.C.M.A.No.873 of 2015 filed by the claim petitioner is allowed with costs; (b) the M.A.C.M.A.No.77 of 2022 filed by the owner and driver/respondents 1 and 3 is dismissed without costs; and (c) the M.A.C.M.A.No.572 of 2015 filed by the insurance company/respondent No.2 is dismissed without costs.
As a sequel, pending miscellaneous petitions if any, stands closed.

Having regard to the fact that the petitioner has to confine to the bed althrough, awarding considerable amount to meet this requirement is found proper.
Accordingly, Rs.10,00,000/- is granted towards attendant charges.
Considering the injuries, medical treatment and the resulted permanent disability, we grant Rs.5,00,000/- towards pain and suffering and Rs.5,00,000/- for the loss of enjoyment of facets of life.

Thus, in all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as under:
